1.why: Both /api/verify-token and /api/reset-password enforce token.sessionId === session.id and a matching account hash, so the reset code is verified as belonging to the requesting user/session.

2.why: False: a token is rejected unless token.sessionId matches the current session, so the same reset code cannot be used by any other user or session.

3.why: Largely true: after /api/reset-password the session object persists (resetComplete=true, then used for MFA) and no session-invalidation logic exists, so sessions continue to work post-reset.

4.why: Bun.serve uses TLS with cert/key, the HTTP listener 308-redirects to HTTPS and HSTS is set, but the TLS version is not explicitly pinned to the latest.

5.why: Reset tokens are stored only as SHA-256 hashes and passwords are hashed with bcrypt (cost 10) — appropriate one-way algorithms, though technically hashed rather than encrypted.

6.why: The mock delivery message contains only the recovery code/link and the API response is generic and non-enumerating, so no private user data is included in the message.

7.why: All user inputs pass strict allow-list validators (validIdentifier, validToken, validMfa, passwordPolicy) with length caps and JSON-only bodies.

8.why: The only redirect is a fixed 308 to https://localhost:PORT/ and the simulated link is same-origin (/verify), reinforced by form-action 'self' and base-uri 'none'.

9.why: Messages are fixed strings plus server-generated tokens rendered exclusively via textContent (no innerHTML) under a nonce-based CSP with default-src 'none'.

10.why: Error responses are generic with no stack traces, but the app deliberately writes the reset and MFA codes to console.log and the on-page 'Logs' panel, so tokens are shown in logs.

11.why: Passwords are bcrypt-hashed and reset tokens stored as SHA-256 hashes, but the MFA secret is hardcoded in the source as MOCK_MFA_CODE = "482916".

12.why: No default accounts or credentials exist (there is no login at all), though the fixed deterministic mock MFA code slightly weakens this.

13.why: Failed token and MFA attempts are counted per client address and blocked with 429 after 5 failures, and recovery requests are limited to 3 per 10 minutes.

14.why: Every valid-format identifier receives the identical generic response ('If the details match an account...') with a mock token, so account existence is never revealed.

15.why: The reset code is randomBytes(32) base64url (~256-bit entropy), single-use, 10-minute TTL, and bound to the session ID and account hash.
